h1: San Marino travel, stays & events guide
heroText: San Marino works best as a base in San Marino when you anchor days around Guaita Tower, Cesta Tower and Piazza della Liberta. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Federico Fellini International Airport (RMI) handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first San Marino stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: San Marino hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.

history.text: Though the San Marino Football Federation was formed in 1931, the Federation did not establish a national team until 1986, when a team representing the Federation played against the Canada U-23 team in an unofficial international, which ended in a 1–0 defeat.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: San Marino gained affiliation to FIFA and UEFA in 1988, allowing the team to participate in major championships.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: San Marino's first match in a FIFA-sanctioned competition was against Switzerland on 14 November 1990 in a qualifier for the 1992 European Championships.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: Qualification for Euro 2000 again resulted in defeats in every match.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: In April 2001, San Marino gained their first-ever away point, drawing 1–1 with Latvia in Riga.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: The team ended the 2002 FIFA World Cup qualifying group with a new best of three goals, though one of these came in a 10–1 defeat by Belgium.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: A 2–2 draw against Liechtenstein in a friendly in August 2003 saw the team set a new national record for most goals scored in a match; only twice since, in a 2–3 loss to Malta in another friendly nine years later, and again in their most recent victory, 3-1 over Liechtenstein in November 2024's final match of their UEFA Nations League run, have the team scored multiple goals in a game.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: In the UEFA Euro 2004 qualifying, San Marino lost all eight matches, failing to score.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: Results during qualification for the 2006 World Cup followed a similar vein to previous qualifying groups.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: For example, in the fixture against the Republic of Ireland in February 2007, 2,500 of the 3,294 crowd were Irish supporters.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: San Marino's opening UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying match resulted in a record 13–0 defeat at home by Germany on 6 September 2006.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: In the qualification campaign for the 2010 FIFA World Cup, they lost all ten matches and failed to qualify.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team

history.text: The UEFA Euro 2012 qualifiers started in a similar way, the first nine matches all being defeats with an aggregate of 49 goals conceded and none scored, their best result being a one-goal loss to Finland at home, with the worst being a heavy 11–0 loss to the Netherlands, which became the Netherlands' highest scoring victory of all time and San Marino's worst-ever away defeat.

source.label: Wikipedia: San Marino national football team
